musts.issue: Rule 19's Type-P/Type-U definition ('a gate fires as Type-P (a positive, checkable pattern was matched...) or Type-U (the gate could not determine a pattern and is refusing on absence-of-evidence grounds)') is a per-instance-verdict framing. The cited evidence card knowledge/harvest_v0.3/base/kc-base-008.yaml defines Type-P/Type-U as a property of the gate's own validation methodology: a gate earns Type-P status only if it has been shown, by construction, to carry BOTH a machine-derived passing control AND a machine-derived failing control; a gate that has only ever demonstrated passing cases (regardless of how many) stays Type-U. This is a claim about how the gate itself was tested/built, not about what a single run's verdict means. The patch silently repurposes the same named law for a different, per-run distinction while citing the same card as its source.
musts.fix: Restate rule 19 to match kc-base-008's actual claim (a gate-construction/validation requirement: 'no gate may be called Type-P until it has demonstrated at least one machine-derived failing control it correctly rejected, in addition to passing controls'), or explicitly mark the per-verdict Type-P/Type-U split as a *new, derived* usage distinct from kc-base-008's original meaning and do not cite kc-base-008 as if it already states this.

FOUNDATION_v0.6_PATCH.md:76 (rule 19) instead defines Type-P/Type-U as a per-firing verdict distinction: 'a gate fires as Type-P (a positive, checkable pattern was matched...) or Type-U (the gate could not determine a pattern and is refusing on absence-of-evidence grounds)' — a statement about what a single run's outcome means, unrelated to whether the gate has ever demonstrated a failing control.

musts.issue: The proposed new citation_card schema field `locators` (array, maxItems 1, 'a single exact_passage may cite at most one contiguous locator; a second, non-adjacent locator... is the composite-quote pattern') does not correspond to any existing field. schema/citation_card.schema.json's actual locator field is `page_or_locator` (a single string) plus `line_or_paragraph` — there is no array-typed `locators` field on disk. The rule as specified therefore proposes a second, competing locator representation rather than extending the one that exists, violating the repo's own one-fact-one-home discipline (REPO_SPEC's own stated principle), and its acceptance-test scenario ('a single citation card whose exact_passage cites two non-adjacent locators, e.g. page 3 and page 47') cannot occur under the current one-citation-card-one-page_or_locator data model as described — the check as written cannot be implemented against the schema that actually exists without first deciding whether page_or_locator becomes multi-valued or whether the composite-quote case is instead detected across two separate citation cards sharing one claim_ref.
musts.fix: Name the actual existing field (`page_or_locator`/`line_or_paragraph`) in the schema-fields block instead of inventing `locators`, and restate the composite-quote detection either as (a) a regex/structural check purely on `exact_passage` (ellipsis/splice markers — this part is fine as specified) plus (b) a cross-card check across multiple citation_card entries sharing the same claim_ref and near-identical exact_passage boundaries, rather than a single non-existent multi-locator field.
